title: Two Russian men jailed in Angola for terrorism and spying
description:
The men were convicted over alleged plan to stage coup and organise deadly demonstrations over fuel prices last year

Two Russian men have been found guilty by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying after being accused of planning a coup and helping to organise deadly demonstrations in the southern African country last year.

Lev Lakshtanov and Igor Ratchin were sentenced to eight and 11 years in jail respectively. They had denied the charges, claiming they were in Angola for cultural and business activities.

Continue reading...
summary: Two Russian men, Lev Lakshtanov and Igor Ratchin, have been convicted by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying, and sentenced to 8 and 11 years in jail respectively, for allegedly planning a coup and organizing deadly demonstrations over fuel prices last year. They had denied the charges, claiming they were in Angola for cultural and business activities. The men were found guilty of these serious crimes.

title: MoD cancels army training in Kenya over powers to prosecute British soldiers
description:
September exercise called off after Kenya raises concerns over funding and jurisdiction for criminal offences

The British army has been forced to cancel training for its troops in Kenya after the Kenyan government refused to ratify a bilateral defence agreement.

While the UK government wanted to renew the existing agreement, Kenyan lawmakers had sought changes to give local authorities greater powers to hold British soldiers accountable for any offences committed in the country.

Continue reading...
summary: The British army has cancelled its training exercise in Kenya due to a dispute over a bilateral defence agreement, with Kenyan lawmakers seeking greater powers to hold British soldiers accountable for any offences committed in the country. The UK government wanted to renew the existing agreement, but Kenyan lawmakers refused to ratify it without changes. The cancellation of the training exercise is a result of this disagreement.

title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC
description:
UK resident was evacuated from Democratic Republic of the Congo where there is an outbreak of the disease

A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.

The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.

Continue reading...
summary: A UK resident who worked in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is being monitored for Ebola in a London hospital after being medically evacuated due to potential exposure to the virus. The worker had been treating patients with the disease in the DRC. The UK Health Security Agency is overseeing the situation.

title: Healthy diet too expensive for one in three people globally, UN report finds
description:
Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025 but experts call for action to bring down costs of fruit, vegetables and dairy as report shows 2.69bn people can’t afford to eat well

One in three people cannot afford to eat a healthy diet, a new report has found, prompting calls for urgent action on food affordability.

There are 2.69 billion people unable to afford a diverse diet that meets their energy and nutrient needs, and it will take “immense” amounts of work to achieve the global target of zero hunger by 2030, the annual report from five UN agencies warned.

Continue reading...
summary: A new UN report found that one in three people globally cannot afford a healthy diet, with 2.69 billion people unable to afford a diverse diet that meets their energy and nutrient needs. This highlights the need for urgent action on food affordability to achieve the global target of zero hunger by 2030. Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025, but experts say more work is needed.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe heads to polls in tense presidential election
description:
Incumbent Carlos Vila Nova hopes to defeat his former party and secure second term as independent

Voters in São Tomé and Príncipe go to the polls for a presidential election on Sunday as one of Africa’s least populous countries seeks to burnish its democratic credentials.

According to the National Election Commission, about 142,000 people are registered to vote in the tiny African state’s elections, approximately 15% of whom live in the diaspora.

Continue reading...
summary: São Tomé and Príncipe is holding a presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent Carlos Vila Nova seeking a second term as an independent candidate. The election is seen as a test of the country's democratic credentials. Approximately 142,000 people are registered to vote.

title: Trump Seems Trapped by Iran War, Even as He Wields the World’s Biggest Hammer
description: A president who thought there were no limits to his power has discovered several, leaving him more frustrated and erratic.
summary: US President Trump is facing limitations in his power, particularly in the context of a potential war with Iran, leading to increased frustration and erratic behavior. This article suggests that Trump's expectations of unlimited power have been challenged.

title: Trump Holds Off on Major War Escalation Against Iran as Advisers Raise Concerns
description: Among the worries is that expanded hostilities could dangerously drain the diminished stockpile of air defense munitions in the Middle East.
summary: US President Trump has decided to hold off on escalating the war against Iran, amid concerns from his advisers that expanded hostilities could deplete the region's air defense munitions. The decision comes as tensions between the US and Iran remain high.

title: U.S.-Iran War Pauses for 2nd Straight Day
description: President Trump put off plans to escalate the fighting in part because of dwindling stockpiles of interceptor missiles, American officials said.
summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict has paused for the second consecutive day, with President Trump deciding not to escalate the situation due to concerns over dwindling missile stockpiles. This decision has brought a temporary reprieve to the escalating tensions between the two nations.

title: E.U. Divided Over Barring Imports From Israeli Settlements
description: The discussion about restricting goods from Israeli settlements in occupied territories reflects a European split over whether and how to confront Israel.
summary: The European Union is divided on whether to ban imports from Israeli settlements in occupied territories, reflecting a split on how to confront Israel. The discussion highlights the EU's internal disagreements on the issue. The move could have significant implications for EU-Israel relations.

title: Inside the Phone-Throwing Drama at the Troubled, Broke Democratic Party
description: The Democrats should be well positioned to make gains in this year’s midterms. But inside party headquarters, every week brings paranoia, worries about money and, on occasion, emotional eruptions.
summary: The Democratic Party is facing internal struggles, including financial concerns and emotional outbursts, ahead of the midterms. Despite being well-positioned to make gains, the party is plagued by paranoia and worries about its financial situation.

title: Andy Burnham rules out early election in exclusive BBC interview
description: The new prime minister told Laura Kuenssberg that people "voted for a manifesto" that he would honour, when pressed on whether there will be an early general election.
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ruled out an early general election, stating that he will honour the manifesto on which he was elected. This decision was made in an exclusive BBC interview with Laura Kuenssberg.

title: Water supply issue affects Gatwick Airport
description: Bottled water is being handed out to passengers and staff while the issue is investigated.
summary: A water supply issue has affected Gatwick Airport, prompting the distribution of bottled water to passengers and staff while the cause is investigated. The airport is taking steps to address the situation. The details of the issue are currently unknown.

title: Firefighters battle wildfire as tens of thousands evacuated near Bordeaux
description: More than 330,000 people have now been evacuated from wildfires across France and Spain.
summary: A massive wildfire is burning near Bordeaux, France, forcing the evacuation of tens of thousands of people, as part of a larger evacuation of over 330,000 people in France and Spain. The situation remains severe, with firefighters battling to contain the blaze.

title: Iran's 'sabre-rattling' should not intimidate UK, Wes Streeting says
description: The defence secretary warns Britain "stands ready to respond to any attacks Iran wishes to wage against this country or our allies".
summary: The UK defence secretary, Wes Streeting, has warned Iran against any potential attacks, stating that the UK is prepared to respond. This comes as a response to Iran's "sabre-rattling" actions. The UK is standing firm in its defense against any potential threats.

title: President Ahmed al-Sharaa: Syria seeking security deal with Israel
description: Syrian President al-Sharaa tells Al Jazeera Damascus seeks a security deal with Israel, and warns of chaos in Lebanon.
summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has announced that Syria is seeking a security deal with Israel, while also warning of potential chaos in Lebanon. The statement was made to Al Jazeera, providing insight into Syria's diplomatic efforts.

title: What is the AI Kill Switch Act proposed in the US and how will it work?
description: US lawmakers introduce a bill aimed at giving the government power to order companies to shut down 'rogue' AI systems.
summary: US lawmakers have proposed a bill, known as the AI Kill Switch Act, which would give the government the authority to order companies to shut down 'rogue' AI systems. The bill aims to provide a mechanism for controlling AI systems that may pose a threat to national security or public safety.

title: Casemiro makes Inter Miami debut despite MLS investigation into transfer
description: Casemiro plays, Messi sits out during his post-World Cup rest, and Suarez scores to give Miami a sixth straight MLS win.
summary: Casemiro made his debut for Inter Miami in a win, while Lionel Messi sat out due to post-World Cup rest and Luis Suarez scored a goal. The team secured their sixth consecutive MLS win.

title: Iran’s army issues warning ahead of Netanyahu’s US visit
description: Iran says it has stopped retaliatory operations in the Gulf, but warns the war could expand if US strikes continue.
summary: Iran has stopped retaliatory operations in the Gulf, but warns that the war could escalate if US strikes continue ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's US visit.

title: ‘No accountability for settler war crimes against Palestinians’
description: ‘No accountability for settler war crimes against Palestinians’
summary: A news article highlights the lack of accountability for war crimes committed by Israeli settlers against Palestinians, raising concerns about the Israeli government's response to these incidents. The article emphasizes the need for justice and accountability in addressing these human rights violations.

title: Police identify suspect after deadly Berlin pride vehicle crash
description: Police asked for information about the whereabouts of a 21-year-old man.
summary: Police have identified a suspect in connection with a deadly vehicle crash during a Berlin pride event, and are seeking information about the individual's whereabouts. The incident resulted in fatalities.

title: LIVE:  ABC News Live
description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events
summary: ABC News Live provides 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events, offering continuous updates and real-time information to viewers. This service aims to keep audiences informed about current events and developments. It serves as a reliable source for news and updates.

title: Iran live updates: Trump met with advisers on Iran options, sources say
description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28, with massive joint U.S.-Israeli strikes.
summary: President Donald Trump announced major combat operations against Iran, with joint U.S.-Israeli strikes, and met with advisers to discuss options. The news is related to the conflict between the U.S. and Iran.

title: Seattle police seek two men who parachuted from the Space Needle
description: Police say two men climbed over the glass wall of Seattle’s iconic Space Needle on Friday, flipped over the edge and parachuted down from the 605-foot structure
summary: Two men were seen parachuting from the Space Needle in Seattle, prompting a police investigation to identify and apprehend the individuals involved. The incident occurred on Friday when the men climbed over the glass wall and jumped off the 605-foot structure.

title: WATCH:  Meet one 'friendly neighbor' who saw someone in need
description: Christopher Hellenthal, still wearing his Spiderman costume from a children's superhero event, rushed into action to help a man in a wheelchair cross the street in Jonesboro, Arkansas.
summary: A man in a Spiderman costume helped a person in a wheelchair cross the street in Jonesboro, Arkansas, showcasing kindness and community spirit. The incident was captured on video and has been shared online. The man's actions have been praised as an example of good Samaritanism.
